## Natural history notes

A fast-moving, slender, nonvenomous snake characterized by its glossy black body, pale chin and throat, and smooth scales. In Florida, it is found in a wide variety of habitats including pine flatwoods, scrub, hardwood hammocks, marsh edges, fields, roadsides, and suburban areas. It is active during the day and feeds on small animals such as lizards, frogs, rodents, insects, birds, and other snakes, often relying on speed to capture prey and escape predators.
